title: Cloud layer: cumulus, stratus, cirrus and mackerel sky
purpose: Generate tileable maps of a cloud layer with alpha: billowing cumulus, an overcast stratus sheet, cirrus streaks, a mackerel sky of puffs in rows or a dark storm, each a distinct density field lit from a sun direction. Use for sky planes and domes, flight and strategy game skies, and backdrops.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python cloud_layer.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: 0 cumulus, 1 stratus, 2 cirrus, 3 mackerel (altocumulus in rows).

parameters.name: coverage
parameters.meaning: Share of the sky covered by cloud.

parameters.name: billow
parameters.meaning: Cauliflower erosion of the cloud edges (cumulus and mackerel).

parameters.name: softness
parameters.meaning: Width of the soft edge between cloud and clear sky.

parameters.name: sun_angle
parameters.meaning: Direction the sunlight comes from across the layer, in turns from +U.

parameters.name: shading
parameters.meaning: Self-shadowing: how dark the far sides and thick cores become.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Fair-weather cumulus: separate white heaps with grey shaded sides.

presets.name: overcast_stratus
presets.description: Overcast stratus: a nearly closed grey sheet with soft thin patches.

presets.name: cirrus_wisps
presets.description: High cirrus: thin bright streaks and hooks across a clear sky.

presets.name: mackerel_sky
presets.description: Mackerel sky: rows of small rounded altocumulus puffs.

presets.name: storm_nimbus
presets.description: Storm: dense dark towering cloud with bright rims, little clear sky.

limits: A flat layer, not volumetric: lighting is a slope term toward the sun with a short sample of cloud in that direction and a darkening of thick cores, so it is an approximation of scattering that suits a sky seen from below or at a distance. The texture tiles, so a wide sky shows the repeat unless two scales are blended. Clouds do not move or change; the albedo alpha suits blending over a sky colour or gradient, and engines sort alpha-blended layers with other transparent surfaces. Height and normals describe density, not real cloud geometry.
technique_references: Fractal noise cut at a coverage quantile
Inverted Worley erosion for billowing edges
Anisotropic and ridged noise warped into cirrus streaks
Cellular puffs modulated by a wave for altocumulus rows
Slope lighting toward a sun direction with a short optical-depth sample
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
